questions.text: A data pipeline defines a global variable tax_rate = 0.08 alongside a modular invoice calculation function. Which statements correctly explain variable scope behavior and data structure properties in this architecture? (Select all that apply)
options: Calling calculate_invoice(100) evaluates using the local tax_rate of 0.10.
Executing calculate_invoice(100) permanently overwrites the global tax_rate value to 0.10.
Immutable data structures such as tuples cannot be modified after creation.
The local tax_rate inside calculate_invoice shadows the global tax_rate within the function’s scope.
questions.explanation: Verified by running it: the call returns 110.0 (so the local 0.10 was used) and the global tax_rate is still 0.08 afterwards. Assigning to a name inside a function creates a new local name and shadows the global one — rebinding the global would need the global keyword. Tuples are immutable.
questions.context:
tax_rate = 0.08 # Global scope variable

def calculate_invoice(subtotal):
    tax_rate = 0.10 # Local scope assignment
    return subtotal + (subtotal * tax_rate)

questions.text: A developer writes a function fibonacci(n) that uses the yield statement to return sequence numbers sequentially. Using yield creates a generator that relies on lazy evaluation to produce values on the fly, preventing system memory from holding large lists.
questions.explanation: True. Verified: a function containing yield returns a generator object, which produces each value on demand rather than building the whole sequence in memory first.

questions.text: An administrator installs speedtest-cli on the virtual machine and later decides to delete the application completely. Running sudo apt-get purge speedtest-cli completely removes the package from the system.
questions.explanation: True. purge removes the package and its configuration files, which is the difference from apt-get remove.

questions.text: A custom greeting script named DataAnalyzer Pro is executed from a Python source file. In what manner does the system process this program?
options: It interprets and executes the source code line by line during runtime.
It transforms the source directly into natural language output.
It converts all source text into machine code binaries prior to execution.
It passes uncompiled text directly to the CPU without intermediate interpretation.
questions.explanation: Python is interpreted: the interpreter reads and executes the source at runtime rather than producing a standalone compiled binary first.

questions.text: Which standard Linux utility is employed to rename an existing file?
questions.explanation: mv moves a file, and moving it within the same directory is how you rename it. rm deletes, cp copies, and dd does low-level block copying.

questions.text: A division function computes a / b. If b = 0, wrapping the computation in a try block with a matching except ZeroDivisionError: block prevents unhandled termination and allows returning an error message.
questions.explanation: True. Verified by running it: 4 / 0 raises ZeroDivisionError, and catching it returns the message instead of crashing.

questions.text: While troubleshooting performance degradation on a server, a system administrator issues the ps command. What data is reported by this command?
options: Active processes and their allocated CPU time
questions.explanation: ps reports the running processes, including accumulated CPU time. Memory totals come from free, disk I/O from iostat, and storage usage from df.

questions.text: A file permission listing for myfile.sh produces the details above. Given the permission string -rwxr-xr--, which two statements correctly summarize the rights granted on this file? (Select two)
options: Members belonging to the self group have full read, write and execute permissions.
All users on the host (others) possess execute privileges.
The file owner with username self has write (modification) rights.
The user account named devasc holds write rights to the file.
Members of the group test have permission to execute the file.
questions.explanation: -rwxr-xr-- is owner rwx, group r-x, others r--, and the listing names the owner as self and the group as test. So the owner can write, and the group can execute but not write. self is a user here rather than a group, others have no execute bit, and devasc does not appear in this listing at all.

questions.text: A network engineer reviews interfaces on a Linux machine using the command ifconfig -a. What output does this flag provide?
options: Displays only interfaces that are currently UP and active.
Displays the kernel IP routing table.
Displays details for both active and inactive interfaces.
Displays the system Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) table.
questions.explanation: -a means all interfaces, including the ones that are down. The routing table is route / ip route, and the ARP table is arp / ip neigh.

questions.text: Which Python control structure keyword allows a program to branch, executing one block when a condition evaluates to true and another block when it does not?
questions.explanation: if, with its optional elif / else branches. def defines a function, from is part of an import, and delay is not a Python keyword at all.

questions.text: An interactive Python prompt initializes the dictionary above. Which expression correctly queries the IP address stored under the key R2?
questions.explanation: Verified: ipAddress["R2"] returns 10.2.2.1. Parentheses raise TypeError (a dict is not callable) and an unquoted R2 raises NameError, because it is read as a variable name.

questions.text: Given the mapping employees = {"1001": "Engineering", "1002": "Marketing"}, evaluating employees["9999"] outside of a try-except block triggers an unhandled KeyError exception that crashes execution.
questions.explanation: True. Verified: square-bracket lookup of a missing key raises KeyError. employees.get("9999") would return None instead of raising.

questions.text: A user creates a file via echo "Linux is AWESOME!" > linux.txt. They intend to duplicate the file as linux2.txt and append content without losing original lines. Which statements regarding redirection operators are accurate? (Select all that apply)
options: Running echo "I LOVE Linux!" > linux2.txt appends text without overwriting existing data.
Running cat linux.txt > linux2.txt creates linux2.txt populated with “Linux is AWESOME!”.
Running echo "Linux is POWERFUL!" > linux.txt overwrites the current contents of linux.txt.
Running echo "I LOVE Linux!" >> linux2.txt appends the string to linux2.txt while preserving prior text.
questions.explanation: Verified by running all four. A single > always truncates the target first — that's exactly why cat linux.txt > linux2.txt copies the file and echo "Linux is POWERFUL!" > linux.txt overwrites it, and why the claim that echo "I LOVE Linux!" > linux2.txt appends without overwriting is wrong. Only >> appends.

questions.text: A Python variable is declared as shown above. Which fundamental Python data type is represented by ipAddress?
questions.explanation: Verified: type(ipAddress).__name__ is dict. Curly braces holding key: value pairs are a dictionary literal; square brackets would be a list and parentheses a tuple.

questions.text: A navigation program declares a coordinate tuple: coordinates = (10.5, 20.0). Later in execution, running coordinates[0] = 12.0 updates the value without throwing an error.
questions.explanation: False. Verified: it raises TypeError: 'tuple' object does not support item assignment. Tuples are immutable — a list would have allowed the assignment.

questions.text: During maintenance on an Ubuntu/Debian system, an administrator executes apt-get upgrade. What does this command accomplish?
options: Each individual application automatically initiates its built-in updater.
Available package and operating system updates are downloaded and installed.
Remote repository package catalog indexes are synced and updated.
questions.explanation: upgrade installs the newest available versions of what is already installed. Syncing the catalogue is the separate apt-get update, which is why the two are normally run in that order.
